notes.summary: Dice and cube questions ask which face is opposite another (from views or an open net), or how many small cubes of a painted cube have 0, 1, 2 or 3 faces painted.

concepts.title: Opposite faces from views
concepts.body: Faces seen together in one view are adjacent, never opposite. A face is opposite the one number that never appears with it. If two views share a common face, the faces in the same position are opposite.

concepts.title: Open net (cube net)
concepts.body: In a straight row of three squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite. Two squares touching each other are adjacent.

concepts.title: Painted cube cut into n × n × n
concepts.body: 3 faces painted = 8 (corners). 2 faces = 12(n − 2). 1 face = 6(n − 2)². No face = (n − 2)³.

varieties.name: Opposite face from positions
varieties.how: List all faces adjacent to the given face; the missing one is opposite.

example.q: Views show 1 with 2, 3, 4 and 5. Which is opposite 1?

varieties.name: Open net
varieties.how: Skip one square in a straight line to find opposite pairs; use them to reject impossible cubes.

example.q: In the net, which number is opposite 3?

varieties.name: Painted cube
varieties.how: Find n (cube root of total pieces), then use the formulas.

example.q: A painted cube is cut into 27 equal cubes. How many have no face painted?

tips: Two faces seen together in any view can never be opposite.
In a net, opposite pairs are found by skipping exactly one square in a straight line.
Corners (3 faces painted) are always 8, whatever n is.
traps: A cube option is wrong if it shows two opposite faces together.
Even with no opposite faces shown, the order around a corner (clockwise vs anticlockwise) can make a cube impossible.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same die are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to 1?
questions.solution:
In both views, 1 is on top.
Faces seen with 1: 2, 3 (view i) and 4, 5 (view ii).
So 2, 3, 4, 5 are adjacent to 1 and the remaining number 6 is opposite 1.

questions.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which number will be on the face opposite to 2?
questions.solution:
2, 3, 4 lie in one straight row. Skip one square: 2 and 4 are opposite.
(Other pairs: 1–5 and 3–6.)

questions.q: A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 64 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
Three different positions of the same die are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to 4?
questions.solution:
View (ii): 4 is with 1 and 2.
View (iii): 4 is with 5 and 6.
So 1, 2, 5, 6 are adjacent to 4. The remaining number, 3, is opposite 4.
(Check: 3 never appears with 4 in any view.)

questions.q: The sheet shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Which of the following cubes can be formed?
questions.solution:
Opposite pairs from the net: 1–5, 2–4, 3–6.
(a) shows 3 and 6 together ✗. (d) shows 1 and 5 together ✗.
(b) and (c) both show 2, 3, 5. Fold the net with 3 on top: 5 is in front, 4 on the right, 2 on the left, 1 at the back.
Turn the cube so 2 is on top (roll it to the right): 3 comes to the right face and 5 stays in front → top 2, front 5, right 3 = cube (b).
Cube (c) has 3 and 5 swapped, which is the mirror arrangement and cannot be made.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted red on all faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have exactly one face painted?
